domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Establish subtraction-ready representation
skills.definition: Prepare quantities for subtraction by rewriting them into a compatible form, including finding a common denominator when needed and normalizing mixed numbers or whole numbers into whole-and-fraction form.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory setup skills that occur before the main subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same problem-solving phase: making the quantities compatible for subtraction. Although they are not identical operations, they are diagnostically close at a coarser level because both are representation-alignment steps rather than execution or post-processing.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract whole-number parts and/or fraction parts once the quantities are in compatible form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because this is the core execution step and has distinct error patterns from setup, regrouping, and finalization.

skills.name: Regroup for subtraction
skills.definition: Borrow 1 from the whole-number part and convert it into fractional units when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because regrouping is a major diagnostic breakpoint with distinctive student errors and does not always occur.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms or convert a zero fractional result to an integer or zero when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is optional in some items and reflects a different cognitive operation from composing the answer.

skills.name: Compose final answer
skills.definition: Combine computed whole-number and fractional parts and express the result in an acceptable final form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final recombination/formatting can succeed or fail independently of simplification and subtraction.
